title: A Martingale Approach To Fluctuations of Rank Estimators in Sensitivity Analysis
summary: Given a bivariate random pair $(X,Y)$, a natural problem is to estimate, from a single sample $(X_i,Y_i)_{1\le i\le n}$, quantities such as $\mathbb{E}\left[ \mathbb{E}[ Y\mid X ]^2 \right]$. More broadly, sensitivity indices are designed to quantify the possibly nonlinear influence of an input variable $X$ on an output variable $Y$. A classical example is the Sobol' index $$ \frac{\mathrm{Var}(\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X])}{\mathrm{Var}(Y)} \in [0,1] \ . $$ Another important example is the Cramér--von Mises (CvM) index.
